headline: Controlled perturbations expose where phylogenetic inference becomes unreliable
label: Phylogenetic Inference Method Evaluation
summary: Simulated hybridization and injected taxon duplicates now quantify where standard phylogenetic inference fails and how support can be calibrated.
synthesis: The dominant thread is benchmarking of phylogenetic inference under conditions where the true answer or noise level can be controlled. Simulations under reticulate evolutionary scenarios show that tree-based comparative methods err on ancestral states, rates and models under hybridization, with the largest errors for fast-evolving traits. The Duplicate Monophyly Criterion uses synthetic taxon duplicates to calibrate distance-matrix noise and yield bootstrap-like support for distance-based structural phylogenies. A third item proposes two maximum likelihood approaches that account for lineage abundance and reports improved inference accuracy on SARS-CoV-2 genomic epidemiology, though it is primarily a method proposal rather than an evaluation. What is new is the use of controlled perturbations, reticulate scenarios and injected duplicates to quantify where standard inference becomes unreliable.
